newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK troop dispute much ado about politics.
newsitem.headline: HK troop dispute much ado about politics.

text.p: Simmering controversy over Beijing's demand to send combat troops to Hong Kong before it returns to Chinese rule has more to do with politics than any military threat, political and military analysts said on Tuesday.

"You can shed a tear for the empire or celebrate Hong Kong's return to China but what you shouldn't do is imagine the place has any great military significance because it doesn't. Hong Kong is an economic powerhouse and a political symbol, that's it," one analyst said.

"All this fuss about whether the Chinese can send a few more troops over the border before the handover has nothing to do with military security. There's no threat to Hong Kong. It's about the end of British sovereignty and the start of China's. It's all political."
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30 after a colonial interlude of more than 150 years.
The Chinese have fewer than 200 unarmed members of their People's Liberation Army (PLA) in place in Hong Kong as an advance party to prepare for the handover.
Beijing had requested permission to send several thousand additional troops over the border prior to the handover, citing the presence of top Chinese leaders at the handover ceremony as one reason.
Britain finally agreed on Monday that 509 PLA troops, most armed with pistols and rifles, could cross the border at 9 pm (0100 GMT) on the 30th.
Observers agree there is no external threat to Hong Kong and that any internal threat is well within the capability of the Hong Kong police.
China is not thought to have any great military need for Hong Kong. Western observers expect Beijing ultimately to deploy fewer than 10,000 troops here along with a small naval complement.
China's blue water ships in the area likely will continue to operate from existing ports in nearby Guandong province.
"Some locations are military assets, some are liabilities and some are of neutral value," said one western military analyst.

"Hong Kong has been a military liability for Britain since before World War Two. The Japanese took Hong Kong in a week. The Chinese could have taken it anytime they wanted since 1949. Even from Beijing's point of view Hong Kong is of neutral value militarily."
Britain will have to negotiate future port visits of its much-reduced naval fleet to Hong Kong on a case-by-case basis.

The United States has an agreement permitting 'R and R' visits by its vessels, which sometimes disgorge as many as 10,000 sailors and marines at a time to swell the coffers of the bars and discos of Wanchai clubland.
U.S. port calls into Hong Kong will continue as a convenience but other locations could and be found if necessary.
"There is only one power in the world other than China that could bring significant force to bear in the area of Hong Kong and that's the United States," one analyst said.
"That's the reality which shapes the politics of this area and that's the reason why Washington has been more important to Hong Kong's future than London for some time now."
